JUDGMENT
The plaintiffs have filed this suit for the relief of permanent injunction with respect to the suit schedule property.

2. It is the case of plaintiffs that originally one Mr.Narayanappa S/o Late Gundappa was the owner of land bearing Sy.No.39/1 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas situated at Nagadevanahalli Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, which was acquired by him under a Registered Sale OS.No.4952/2021 Deed dated 02.08.1961.
Since the date of purchase, the above said Narayanappa was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the above said property.
The B.D.A (Bengaluru Development Authority) had acquired the above said land on 19.01.1989 for the purpose of formation of "Jnanabharathi Layout".
Ultimately, the B.D.A had issued Final Notification on 19.01.1994 U/s.19 of B.D.A. Act, finalizing the acquisition proceedings.
However, the B.D.A has failed to take the possession of the above said property and also failed to implement the scheme.
Therefore, Narayanappa remained as absolute owner of the above said property.
Out of 1 acre 8 guntas of land, Narayanappa has carved out five sites in eight guntas and sold the same to different persons.
The plaintiffs have purchased the sites from Narayanappa or from the purchasers who have purchased the sites from Narayanappa.
3. The plaintiff No.1 had purchased the site measuring East to West 60 feet and North to South 25 feet by virtue of a Registered Sale Deed dated 29.04.2009.
The plaintiff No.2 had purchased the site measuring East to West 60 feet and North to South 25 feet by virtue of Registered Sale Deed dated 06.06.2012 from one Smt.P.V.Anitha.
The said Smt.P.V.Anitha had purchased the said site from one Narayanappa on 29.04.2009.
The plaintiff No.3 had purchased the site measuring East to West 30 feet and North to South 40 feet by OS.No.4952/2021 virtue of Registered Sale Deed dated 15.11.1997 from Narayanappa.
The plaintiff No.4 and 5 have jointly purchased the site measuring East to West 30 feet and North to South 45 feet by virtue of Registered Sale Deed dated 24.01.2013 from Narayanappa.
The plaintiff No.6 had purchased the site measuring East to West 30 feet and North to South 40 feet by virtue of Registered G.P.A. dated 12.12.1996 from Narayanappa.
Since the date of purchase, the plaintiffs are in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule sites as absolute owners.
They have obtained Electricity Connections from BESCOM and all other basic amenities required for the dwelling house.
The plaintiffs have put up construction over their respective sites.
All of a sudden, the B.D.A has issued notice to the plaintiffs on 26.03.2014 U/s.32 of B.D.A. Act, stating that they have put up illegal construction.
The notice have been suitably replied by the plaintiffs.
The B.D.A had attempted to evict the plaintiffs from the suit schedule property.
Therefore, the plaintiffs have approached the Hon'ble High Court in WP.No.3099- 3103/2016 and obtained a stay order.
The defendants never came near the suit schedule property until the stay order passed by Hon'ble High Court.

The defendants claiming themselves as the legal heirs of Narayanappa S/o Gundappa came near the suit schedule properties for the first time on 12.06.2021 and attempted to disturb the possession of the OS.No.4952/2021 plaintiffs and also attempted to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit schedule properties

On 16.08.2021, the defendants came near the suit schedule properties along with some persons who claimed themselves to be revenue officials Shanaz vs Patlappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2028041/
3 and rowdy elements and attempted to measure the land.
The plaintiffs resisted the same by taking assistance of the police.
In view of the above said interference of the defendants to the possession of the plaintiffs, they are constrained to file the present suit for the relief of permanent injunction.
4. After institution of the suit summons was issued to the defendants.
In pursuance of summons, the defendants No.1 to 4 appeared before the court through their counsel.
The defendants No.1, 3 to 5 filed their written statement.

The defendant No.2 filed memo adopting the written statement filed by the defendants No.1, 2 to 5.
5.
In their written statement, the defendants have categorically denied the averments made in the plaint.
It is further contended that the plaintiffs have no locus-standi to file the suit.
The suit is barred by limitation.
There is no cause of action for the suit, the court fee paid is improper, the plaintiffs have not approached the court with clean hand and suppressed the material facts.

It is further submitted that originally Late Narayanappa S/o.Gundappa was the owner of OS.No.4952/2021 Sy.No.39/1 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas situated at Nagadevanhalli Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk, which was purchased by him under a Registered Sale Deed dated 02.08.1961 from one Doddamma and thereafter he had put up shed in the said property in the year 2000.
Narayanappa had one son who is defendant No.1 and a daughter by name Saraswathi.
Narayanappa and Saraswathi are no more.
The defendants No.2 to 4 are the legal heirs of Late Saraswathi.
The B.D.A had acquired land bearing Sy.No.39/1 as per Preliminary Notification No.BDA/ALAO/A3/139/88-89 dated 19.01.1989 for the purpose of formation of Jnanabharathi Layout.
The B.D.A issued final notification on 19.01.1994.
On the basis of the said notification Sri.Narayanappa lost his right, title, interest and possession over the said property.
But the B.D.A failed to take possession and form the layout.
Therefore, Narayanappa got de-notified the land from B.D.A.
During the pendency of process of de-notification, Narayanappa died on 25.06.2002 leaving behind these defendants as Class-I heirs.
As per de- notification, 1 acre has fallen to H.Suresh Kamath and remaining 8 guntas fallen to the defendants.
These defendants are in possession and enjoyment of Sy.No.39/1/4 of Nagadevanahalli Village measuring 8 guntas.
On 17.04.2021, the defendants have divided the above said property amongst themselves as per the Registered Partition OS.No.4952/2021 Deed dated 17.04.2021.
Accordingly, the defendants are in possession of their respective share and paying taxes.
All the revenue records are standing in the name of defendants and they are in possession and enjoyment of the same.

When such being the case, the plaintiffs who are strangers and who have no manner of right, title or interest over the suit schedule property came near the suit schedule properties on 10.07.2021 at about 10.00 a.m, and attempted to interfere with the defendants peaceful possession and enjoyment with the help of created and concocted documents.
The defendants resisted the act of the plaintiffs.
As the police officials did not come to the rescue of the defendants they have filed in OS.No.5538/2021 on the file of CCH-18 and got interim stay.
Late Narayanayappa has not executed any documents during his life time.
As the property was vested with B.D.A from 1994 to 2021, Narayanappa had no right to execute any deed in favour of any one.
The plaintiffs have not questioned the revenue documents standing in the name of these defendants.
The plaintiffs are the land grabbers who have created the documents in collusion with the Government officials and attempting to dispossess the defendants from the suit schedule property.
On the above said grounds, the defendants have prayed this court to dismiss the suit of the plaintiffs.

REASONS 11. ISSUES NO.1 to 5 :- These issues are taken up together for consideration to avoid repetition of facts.
12. Order 20 Rule 5 of CPC mandates that a court when delivering judgment is required to provide a specific finding or decision on each issue framed in a case, but on perusal of issue No.1 to 5 it is found that the said issues are framed in OS.No.4952/2021 respect of possession of plaintiffs as on the date of the suit. Therefore, the said issues have been taken up for consideration together.

13. Before considering whether the plaintiffs have proved their possession over the suit schedule property as on the date of suit or not, it is pertinent to note that, there is no dispute among the parties regarding lawful ownership of Late Narayanappa S/o.Gundappa with respect to land bearing Sy.No.39/1 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas situated at Nagadevanahalli Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk.
It is also not in dispute that the above said property was acquired by B.D.A in the year 1989 for the purpose of formation of Jnanabharathi Layout.
It is also not in dispute that as the B.D.A was unable to execute work of formation of layout, the land was de-notified.
Sec.38 of the Specific Relief Act proposes circumstances under which a order of permanent injunction can be granted.

For the sake of convenience Sec.38 of Specific Reflief Act is extracted below ;-
38. Perpetual injunction when granted.--

"(1)Subject to the other provisions contained in or referred to by this Chapter, a perpetual injunction may be granted to the plaintiff to prevent the breach of an obligation existing in his favour, whether expressly or by implication.
(2)When any such obligation arises from contract, the court shall be guided by the rules and OS.No.4952/2021 provisions contained in Chapter II.

(3)When the defendant invades or threatens to invade the plaintiff's right to, or enjoyment of, property, the Shanaz vs Patlappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2028041/
6 court may grant a perpetual injunction in the following cases, namely:--
(a)where the defendant is trustee of the property for the plaintiff;(b)where there exists no standard for ascertaining the actual damage caused, or likely to be caused,
by the invasion;(c)where the invasion is such that compensation in money would not afford adequate relief;(d)where the injunction is necessary to prevent a multiplicity of judicial proceedings."
14. Keeping in mind the above said provision of law let me appreciate whether the plaintiffs have successfully proved their lawful possession over the suit schedule properties as on the date of suit.

15. The plaintiffs are claiming that they have purchased sites formed in Sy.No.39/1 from Sri.Narayanappa or from the owners who had purchased the sites from the purchasers or the power of attorney holder of Narayanappa and his two sons.
On the other hand, it is the specific defense of the defendants that Narayanappa had no authority to execute the sale deeds as the land bearing Sy.No.39/1 was acquired by the B.D.A.
In order to establish the case of the plaintiffs, the plaintiff No.3 by name Sri.Allabakash S/o.Mohammad Masood stepped into witness box and examined himself as OS.No.4952/2021 PW-1.
The examination in chief of PW-1 is the verbatim of the averments made in the plaint.

Ex.P-1 is the Digital copy of the Registered Sale Deed dated 29.04.2009, Ex.P-2 is the Digital copy of the Sale Deed dated 06.06.2012, Ex.P.3 is the Digital copy of the Sale Deed dated 15.11.1997, Ex.P-4 is the Digital copy of Sale Deed dated 24.1.2012, Ex.P-5 to 11 are the Encumbrance Certificates, Ex.P-12 to 14 are the Electricity Bills, Ex.P-15 is the Electricity Bill, Ex.P-16 to 19 are the Tax Receipts, Ex.P-20 to 23 are the Consent Deeds executed by two sons of late Narayanappa by name Satynarayana and Patlappa in favour of the plaintiffs confirming the sale deeds executed by Narayanappa or his power of attorney holder by name Shoukat and Abdul Kareem.
16. I have carefully gone through the oral and documentary evidence placed on record.
As already discussed in the earlier part of this judgment, there is no dispute with respect to the fact that Narayanappa was the owner of the suit schedule properties.
The plaintiffs are contending that they came into possession of the suit schedule properties under registered sale deeds.

17. Ex.P-1 is the Digital copy of registered sale deed executed by one Showkath S/o.Mohammad Mahaboob the OS.No.4952/2021 GPA holder of Sri.Narayanappa and his two sons by name Satyanarayana and Patlappa.
Ex.P-2 is the Digital copy of the registered sale deed executed by GPA holder of Narayanappa and his two sons in favour of plaintiff No.2.
Ex.P-3 is the Digital copy of registered sale deed executed by Sri.Abdul Kareem who is again GPA holder of Narayanappa and his two sons in favour of plaintiff No.3.
Ex.P-4 is the Digital copy of registered sale deed dated 24.01.2012 in favour of plaintiff No.4 by the GPA holder of Narayanappa and his two sons by name Mohammad Mahaboob.
Ex.P-16 to 19 are the Khata Extracts standing in the name of the plaintiffs.
It is not the contention of the defendants that the GPA holder had no authority to execute sale deeds in favour of plaintiffs or the vendors.
But it is their case that in view of acquisition of Sy.No.39/1 by the B.D.A Sri.Narayanappa had no authority to execute sale deeds in favour of anyone.

As already discussed in the earlier part of this judgment, though the land was acquired by B.D.A the same was Shanaz vs Patlappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2028041/
7 de-notified by the Government when B.D.A failed to execute the project for the purpose of which the land was acquired.
If the Government acted U/s.48 of Land Acquisition Act and de-notified the land, then Sri.Narayanappa and his sons were deemed to be in possession of the suit schedule land i.e. Sy.No.39/1.
When such being the case, the original owner will be capable of delivering the suit schedule property as per his wish.

At this OS.No.4952/2021 juncture, it is relevant to refer to the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between K.G.Srinivasa v/s the Government of Karnataka decided on 01.10.2012 while considering de-notification U/s.48 of Land Acquisition Act has observed as under;-
"As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioners, if once de-notification was ordered U/s.48(1) of the LA Act, it would presuppose that possession was never taken of the land and that the land had not vested in the state.

entities.text: K.G.Srinivasa v/s the Government of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is only then that the question of de- notification would arise.
The de-notification having been published in the Gazette would have its effect of declaring that the land has been duly de- notified since possession was not taken of the same.

The action of the State Government to thereafter withdraw the order of de-notification cannot be countenanced in law, though it was always open for the State Government under its power of eminent domain to notify the lands, if it was required for a public purpose and to initiate fresh proceedings and to acquire the same.

The process of issuing de-notification and then withdrawing the notification is not a measure that would be legal as once the land is de-notified, the rights of the land owner would revive and stand restored.
This is neither contemplated U/s.48 of the LA Act nor would it stand to commonsense.

Therefore the same cannot be sustained".
18.

The above said observation of Hon'ble High Court makes it clear that when land is de-notified,
then the original owners will be deemed in possession of the property.
Therefore, there OS.No.4952/2021 is no impediment to transfer the property to others.

19. In order to demonstrate their lawful possession, the plaintiffs apart from producing the sale deeds have also produced the khata extracts which are marked as Ex.P-16 to Ex.P-19 which are standing in the name of the plaintiffs.
Ex.P-20 to Ex.P-23 are the consent deeds executed by sons of Narayanappa by name Satyanarayana and Patlappa in favour of the plaintiffs.
Ex.P-20 to Ex.P-23 do not convey any right in themselves.
Therefore, they are not required to be registered.
The digital copy of the registered sale deeds, the Electricity Bills and the khata extracts would establish lawful possession of the plaintiffs over the suit schedule properties.

The defendants who have filed their written statement have failed to produce any contra material before the court to show that they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of this suit.

The sale deed which are standing in the name of the plaintiffs are of the year 29.04.2009, 06.06.2012,
29-04-2009, 15.11.1997, 24.01.2013, 12.12.1996.
The defendants have not questioned the sale deed standing in the name of the plaintiffs till the year 2021.

That means to say that the plaintiffs are in settled possession of the suit schedule properties since long time on the basis of the registered sale deed which have got evidentiary value in the eye of law.

The consent deeds OS.No.4952/2021 executed by the sons of Narayanappa in favour of the plaintiffs which are marked at Ex.P-20 to Ex.P-23 have ratified the lawful possession and enjoyment of the plaintiffs over the suit schedule Shanaz vs Patlappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2028041/
8 properties.

For all the reasons stated above, I am of the opinion that the plaintiffs have proved that they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule properties as pleaded in the plaint as on the date of the suit.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 to 5 in the Affirmative.

20. ISSUE NO.6 :- The plaintiffs in their plaint have specifically contended that the defendants came near the suit schedule properties claiming themselves to be the LRs of late Narayanappa on 12.06.2021 and illegally attempted to interfere with their peaceful possession and enjoyment and also attempted to dispossess them from the suit schedule properties.

On the other hand, the defendants in their written statement have claimed that the plaintiffs have attempted to interfere with their peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property in the year 2021 on the basis of created and concocted documents.
The examination in chief of PW-1 to 3 regarding illegal interference by the defendants has gone unchallenged.

The defense raised by the defendants claiming themselves to be in possession of the suit schedule property as on the date of the suit makes itself clear that the defendants have attempted to interfere OS.No.4952/2021 with the peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as claimed by the plaintiffs.
The consent deeds executed by defendant No.1 and another son of Narayanappa ratifies the lawful possession and enjoyment of the defendants over the suit schedule property.

Therefore, I have no hesitation to come to the conclusion that the plaintiffs have proved that the defendants have attempted to interfere with the plaintiffs peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property.
Hence, I answer Issue No.6 in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.7 :- The defendants in their written statement have raised the contention that suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable without seeking the relief of declaration.
In view of the above said contention, the Issue No.7 has been framed.
The plaintiffs have claimed that they came into possession of the suit schedule property by virtue of registered sale deed executed by Narayanappa and his two sons or his power of attorney holders.

As already discussed in the earlier part of this judgment, the plaintiffs have proved their lawful possession over the suit schedule properties with the help of registered documents as well as the revenue documents, Electricity bills as well as khata extracts pertaining to the suit schedule properties.
Here is a case wherein there is no dispute with respect to ownership of land OS.No.4952/2021 bearing Sy.No.39/1 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas.

The defendants have claimed that as the suit schedule properties was acquired by the B.D.A for the formation of a layout, Narayanappa had no authority to execute the sale deed in favour of the plaintiffs.

This court while answering Issue No.1 to 6 has clearly opined that when once the land bearing Sy.No.39/1 was de-notified, then the original owners or his LRs as the case may be will be in deemed possession and enjoyment of the land bearing Sy.No.39/1.
No further documents is required to prove the re-delivery of possession after the de-notification.
Therefore, there is no cloud of doubt with respect to the land bearing Sy.No.39/1 measuring 1 acre 8 guntas.

At this juncture, it is relevant rely on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in (2009) 4 SCC 594 between Anathulla Sudhakar V/s P.Buchireddy (Dead) by the LRs and others wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has given a clear finding regarding the fact when a suit for bare injunction would not be maintainable.

entities.text: Anathulla Sudhakar V/s P.Buchireddy (Dead) by the LRs and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court is as under :-
" 13.

In a suit for permanent injunction to restrain the defendant from interfering with plaintiff's possession, the plaintiff will have to establish that as on the date of the Shanaz vs Patlappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2028041/
9 suit he was in lawful possession of the suit property and defendant tried to interfere or disturb such lawful possession.
Where the property is a building or building with appurtenant land, OS.No.4952/2021 there may not be much difficulty in establishing possession.
The plaintiff may prove physical or lawful possession, either of himself or by him through his family members or agents or lessees/licensees.
Even in respect of a land without structures, as for example an agricultural land, possession may be established with reference to the actual use and cultivation.
The question of title is not in issue in such a suit, though it may arise incidentally or collaterally.
14. But what if the property is a vacant site, which is not physically possessed, used or enjoyed?
In such cases the principle is that possession follows title.
If two persons claim to be in possession of a vacant site, one who is able to establish title thereto will be considered to be in possession, as against the person who is not able to establish title.

This means that even though a suit relating to a vacant site is for a mere injunction and the issue is one of possession, it will be necessary to examine and determine the title as a prelude for deciding the de jure possession.

In such a situation, where the title is clear and simple, the court may venture a decision on the issue of title, so as to decide the question of de jure possession even though the suit is for a mere injunction."
"But persons having clear title and possession suing for injunction, should not be driven to the costlier and more cumbersome OS.No.4952/2021 remedy of a suit for declaration, merely because some meddler vexatiously or wrongfully makes a claim or tries to encroach upon his property.

The court should use its discretion carefully to identify cases where it will enquire into title and cases where it will refer to plaintiff to a more comprehensive declaratory suit, depending upon the facts of the case."
22.
On careful perusal of the observation of Hon'ble Apex Court it becomes clear that in the present case there is no cloud of doubt with respect to the ownership of the property.
Therefore, the contention of the defendants that the suit for bare injunction without seeking the relief of declaration is not maintainable does not hold any water.

Apart from it, the defendants in their written statement themselves have contended that they have already filed a comprehensive suit for declaration against the plaintiffs in OS.5538/2021 before CCH-18.
In view of the above said contention it can be said that the above said court will consider the title of the property in the above said comprehensive suit.
Apart from it, the defendants have failed to adduced any rebuttal evidence as per the defense taken in the written statement.

Therefore, I have no hesitation to hold that the defendants have failed to prove that the suit of the plaintiffs for the relief of injunction without seeking the relief of declaration is not maintainable.
Hence, I answer Issue No.7 in the Negative.
23. ISSUE NO.8 :-
As already discussed while answering Issue No.1 to 6, the plaintiffs are found in possession of suit schedule property as on the date of filing of the suit.

Apart from it even if we consider the fact that the plaintiffs came in possession of the suit schedule property on the basis of Shanaz vs Patlappa on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/2028041/
10 defective title, then also they settled possession has to be protected till they are evicted with the help of due process of law.
For all the reasons stated above, I am of the opinion that, the plaintiffs are entitled to get the relief as prayed for in the plaint.
Hence, I answer Issue No.8 in the Affirmative.

24. ISSUE NO.9 :- In view of my findings on Issue No.1 to 8, I proceed to pass the following :-
ORDER
The suit of the plaintiffs is hereby decreed.

Consequently, the defendants,
their agents, servants or legal heirs or anybody claiming under them are hereby permanently restrained from interfering with the plaintiffs peaceful possession and enjoyment of their respective sites as mentioned in the suit schedule by an order of permanent injunction.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, there is no order as to costs.
OS.No.4952/2021 Office is directed to draw decree accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The B.D.A (Bengaluru Development Authority) had acquired the above said land on 19.01.1989 for the purpose of formation of "Jnanabharathi Layout".
Ultimately, the B.D.A had issued Final Notification on 19.01.1994 U/s.19 of B.D.A. Act, finalizing the acquisition proceedings.
However, the B.D.A has failed to take the possession of the above said property and also failed to implement the scheme.
Since the date of purchase, the plaintiffs are in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule sites as absolute owners.
The plaintiffs have put up construction over their respective sites.
All of a sudden, the B.D.A has issued notice to the plaintiffs on 26.03.2014 U/s.32 of B.D.A. Act, stating that they have put up illegal construction.
The B.D.A had attempted to evict the plaintiffs from the suit schedule property.
The defendants never came near the suit schedule property until the stay order passed by Hon'ble High Court.
The plaintiffs resisted the same by taking assistance of the police.
The B.D.A issued final notification on 19.01.1994.
On the basis of the said notification Sri.Narayanappa lost his right, title, interest and possession over the said property.
But the B.D.A failed to take possession and form the layout.
Therefore, Narayanappa got de-notified the land from B.D.A.
During the pendency of process of de-notification, Narayanappa died on 25.06.2002 leaving behind these defendants as Class-I heirs.
Accordingly, the defendants are in possession of their respective share and paying taxes.
When such being the case, the plaintiffs who are strangers and who have no manner of right, title or interest over the suit schedule property came near the suit schedule properties on 10.07.2021 at about 10.00 a.m, and attempted to interfere with the defendants peaceful possession and enjoyment with the help of created and concocted documents.
The defendants resisted the act of the plaintiffs.
As the police officials did not come to the rescue of the defendants they have filed in OS.No.5538/2021 on the file of CCH-18 and got interim stay.
As the property was vested with B.D.A from 1994 to 2021, Narayanappa had no right to execute any deed in favour of any one.
The plaintiffs are the land grabbers who have created the documents in collusion with the Government officials and attempting to dispossess the defendants from the suit schedule property.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On the other hand, it is the specific defense of the defendants that Narayanappa had no authority to execute the sale deeds as the land bearing Sy.No.39/1 was acquired by the B.D.A.
Therefore, they are not required to be registered.
The digital copy of the registered sale deeds, the Electricity Bills and the khata extracts would establish lawful possession of the plaintiffs over the suit schedule properties.
The defendants who have filed their written statement have failed to produce any contra material before the court to show that they are in lawful possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as on the date of this suit.
The sale deed which are standing in the name of the plaintiffs are of the year 29.04.2009, 06.06.2012,
29-04-2009, 15.11.1997, 24.01.2013, 12.12.1996.
The defendants have not questioned the sale deed standing in the name of the plaintiffs till the year 2021.
That means to say that the plaintiffs are in settled possession of the suit schedule properties since long time on the basis of the registered sale deed which have got evidentiary value in the eye of law.
The consent deeds executed by defendant No.1 and another son of Narayanappa ratifies the lawful possession and enjoyment of the defendants over the suit schedule property.
Therefore, I have no hesitation to hold that the defendants have failed to prove that the suit of the plaintiffs for the relief of injunction without seeking the relief of declaration is not maintainable.

ORDER
The suit of the plaintiffs is hereby decreed.
Consequently, the defendants,
their agents, servants or legal heirs or anybody claiming under them are hereby permanently restrained from interfering with the plaintiffs peaceful possession and enjoyment of their respective sites as mentioned in the suit schedule by an order of permanent injunction.
Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, there is no order as to costs.
